title: Named by deeds (Exodus Rabbah 3:6)
hookLine: God tells Moses: I am named according to My deeds
tomorrow: why does Moses, of all people, stumble over words?

cards: At a retirement party, nobody reads out a résumé. They tell stories: she never missed one of my games; he always stopped to fix the neighbor's gate. The title fades, and the deeds become the name.
At the burning bush, Moses asks the name question. When the people ask who sent me, what do I tell them?

teach.b: God's answer in Exodus is well-known and mysterious: "I AM THAT I AM." Exodus Rabbah hears it as an answer about deeds. Rabbi Abba bar Mammel says: the Holy One told Moses, you want to know My name?
I am called according to My deeds. When I judge the world, I'm called Elohim. When I go out against the wicked, Tzevaot, hosts.
When I hold back judgment on people's wrongs, El Shaddai.
And when I have mercy on My world, I'm called by the holy name, the one read aloud in prayer as Adonai.
So I am that I am becomes: I am what I do.
The names change because the deeds change. That turns a big question around. Asking God's name, in this midrash, means asking what God does.
And if even God is known by deeds, it's no wonder people are too. A name, on this reading, isn't the label on the door.
It's the shape of what someone keeps doing: the one who shows up, the one who fixes things, the one who forgives. Names get earned in the doing, a day at a time.

how: Jewish prayer uses several names of God, and Jews traditionally do not pronounce the holy four-letter name, reading it aloud as Adonai in prayer and often as HaShem, the Name, outside it.

o: known by what you do, not by your label
a Hebrew name given to a baby at birth
a title earned by passing a hard exam

games.q: which name, which deed — tap the pairs.
p: when God goes out against the wicked
how the name of mercy is read aloud

s: God has one fixed name in the Torah
the midrash lists several, each tied to a different deed.
Exodus Rabbah reads I am that I am as being about deeds
I am called according to My deeds.
a name tells you what someone is, not what they do
this midrash says even God is named by deeds.

games.q: a friend is stressing about the title on her new job. by this midrash, what makes her name?
o: the deeds she keeps doing, day after day.
the title on her door and her business card.
the name her parents chose, which never changes.
games.why: Rabbi Abba bar Mammel: even God says, I am called according to My deeds.

practice: Bring to mind three people you love, one at a time. For each, skip the job or the title and name one thing they do, the deed you'd tell at their party, counting them on your fingers.
Then, gently, wonder which deed you'd like to be named for.

wordCard.voice: Named by deeds: Exodus Rabbah's reading of I am that I am. God is called by what God does: judging, holding back, mercy.

orig.note: Hebrew: I will be, from I am that I am (Exodus 3:14), read as named by deeds.

carryVoice: Your line: named by deeds. A name gets earned in the doing. Day fifteen eighty.

sources.ref: Exodus Rabbah 3:6 (Rabbi Abba bar Mammel: 'I am called according to My deeds': Elohim, Tzevaot, El Shaddai, the holy name)
